description: The Mauryan Empire was the first pan-Indian empire in ancient India. It was founded by Chandragupta Maurya and reached its zenith under Ashoka the Great, who adopted the policy of Dhamma (non-violence and morality) instead of conquest by war.

sections.title: Origin and Early Rulers
sections.description: The foundation and early expansion of the Mauryan Empire under Chandragupta Maurya and Bindusara.

historical_events.significance: Chandragupta Maurya, with the guidance of Chanakya, defeated Dhana Nanda and established the Mauryan Empire.
Chandragupta defeated the Greek General Seleucus Nicator, securing control over territories in present-day Afghanistan and Balochistan.

important_facts.fact: The capital of the empire was Pataliputra (modern-day Patna, Bihar).
Chandragupta Maurya embraced Jainism towards the end of his life and died by Santhara (fasting unto death) at Shravanabelagola in Karnataka.
Bindusara, son of Chandragupta, was a patron of the Ajivika sect and was known by the Greeks as 'Amitraghata' (Slayer of Enemies).

sections.title: Ashoka the Great and Kalinga War
sections.description: The reign of Emperor Ashoka, his military campaigns, and the subsequent spread of Dhamma.

key_concepts.explanation: It was not a new religion, but a moral code based on non-violence (Ahimsa), tolerance, respect for elders, and welfare of the people.

historical_events.significance: The massive bloodshed in this war led to Ashoka's profound change of heart, prompting him to abandon military conquest and embrace Buddhism.

key_associations.extra_info: Most of the Ashokan inscriptions refer to him by this title, which translates to 'Beloved of the Gods'.
Upagupta is credited with initiating Emperor Ashoka into Buddhism.

sections.title: Mauryan Administration and Economy
sections.description: The highly centralized governance system, administrative divisions, and revenue models of the Mauryan period.

key_concepts.explanation: The King was the supreme authority, assisted by a Council of Ministers known as the 'Mantriparishad'.
The 18 highest officials in the administration were called 'Tirthas', while the heads of 27 various economic and state departments were known as 'Adhyakshas'.

important_facts.fact: The empire was divided into provinces ruled by royal princes who were designated as 'Kumaras' or 'Aryaputras'.
The primary currency of the Mauryan economy was the 'Pana', a punch-marked silver coin.
The main source of state revenue was the land tax (Bhaga), which was generally fixed at 1/6th of the total agricultural produce.

sections.title: Important Literary Sources
sections.description: Key historical texts that are instrumental in reconstructing the history of the Mauryan Empire.

key_associations.extra_info: A comprehensive treatise written in Sanskrit covering statecraft, economic policy, administration, and military strategy.
Written by the Greek ambassador to Chandragupta's court, it provides detailed accounts of Mauryan society, administration, and the city of Pataliputra.
A Sanskrit play written during the Gupta period that narrates the political maneuvers of Chanakya to overthrow the Nanda Dynasty.

sections.title: Art, Architecture and Decline of the Empire
sections.description: The physical remnants of Mauryan art and the factors leading to the fall of the empire.

key_concepts.explanation: Royal orders and moral teachings were carved on rocks and polished sandstone pillars to communicate directly with the public, primarily using the Prakrit language and Brahmi script.

important_facts.fact: The Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath, featuring four Asiatic lions, was adopted as the National Emblem of India.
The foundation of the Great Stupa at Sanchi (Madhya Pradesh) was originally laid by Emperor Ashoka.
In 1837, British scholar and antiquary James Prinsep successfully deciphered the Brahmi script used in Ashokan edicts for the first time.
The Mauryan Empire came to an end in 185 BCE when the last emperor, Brihadratha, was assassinated by his own commander-in-chief, Pushyamitra Shunga, establishing the Shunga Dynasty.
